name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
native: กรุงเทพทวารวดีศรีอยุธยา (Krung Thep Dvaravati Si Ayutthaya)

predecessors.name: Lavo Kingdom
predecessors.text: Lopburi and Ayodhya, the Lavo core

predecessors.name: Phip Phli
predecessors.text: Phip Phli (Phetchaburi), named in the infobox among the predecessors

successors.name: Thonburi Kingdom
successors.text: Phraya Tak 'reconquered Ayutthaya-Thonburi area in November 1767' and was 'newly enthroned as King Taksin in December 1767' at Thonburi

successors.name: Konbaung dynasty
successors.text: Siam lost Tenaserim to Burma for perpetuity in 1765

ledger.x: 1351: the Ayutthaya Kingdom is founded.
1353: Ayutthaya takes Angkor and sets its princes on the Khmer throne.
1357: the Khmers retake Angkor.
1370: Borommarachathirat of Suphanburi takes Ayutthaya from Ramesuan of Lopburi, who withdraws to Lavo.
1375: Cliopatria draws a large western strip of the Khmer Empire as Ayutthaya's (212 of the 909 new cells lie in the Khmer outline of 1374).

1375: Cliopatria extends Ayutthaya over the Khorat plateau, the Malay peninsula down to Nakhon Si Thammarat and the Tenasserim coast: 680 cells of Cliopatria's Sukhothai outline of 1374 (which shrinks to a 215-cell northern core in 1375).
1375: the last 13 cells of Cliopatria's Lavo outline pass to Ayutthaya's shape.
1378: Lue Thai of Sukhothai submits as an Ayutthayan vassal.
1388: Ramesuan recovers Ayutthaya and Lavo is fully incorporated.
1388: Ramesuan, the Lopburi king, is back on the throne of Ayutthaya, after Borommarachathirat's line (1370) and Thong Lan.
1393: Ramesuan besieges Angkor again.
1394: Angkor falls to Ayutthaya.
1408: the Suphannabhum line regains the throne under Intharacha ('the Suphannabhum line regains the throne under Intharacha').
1431: Siamese forces take Angkor and seat a puppet.
1432: the Cambodians recover their capital.
1438: the tribute ends in annexation.
1438: Ayutthaya annexes Sukhothai.
1441: the Ayutthaya-Lan Na War begins with 'the Ayutthayan invasion of southern Lan Na'.
1451: Sawankhalok breaks away to Lan Na.
1452: Ayutthaya takes Chiang Mai.
1452: Ayutthaya withdraws from Chiang Mai; the page gives no reason.
1453 (placeholder for 1452-1458): Sawankhalok rejoins Ayutthaya.
1459: Lan Na captures Sawankhalok again.
1459: Cliopatria adds the far south (Songkhla, Satun, Pattani: 32 cells, 18 of them in Kedah's outline).
1460: Ayutthaya reconquers Phrae.
1463: Borommatrailokkanat makes Phitsanulok the principal capital (infobox: Phitsanulok 1463-c.1488; the Sukhothai page: 'In 1463 Borommatrailokkanat moved the royal residence to Song Khwae').
1474: the war ends in stalemate.
1474: Ayutthaya takes Sawankhalok back.
c. 1488: the court returns to Ayutthaya (infobox: Ayutthaya 1488-early 1680s, Phitsanulok principal capital until c.1488).
1512 (Cliopatria's year): the Patani region is a tributary of Ayutthaya, drawn as a tint, not direct land.
1563: the Northern Cities fall to Toungoo as tributaries.
1563: Patani breaks with Ayutthaya.
1564: Ayutthaya surrenders to Bayinnaung and its western strip (Tenasserim, the Mon uplands) passes to Toungoo.
1568: Ayutthaya revolts and attacks Phitsanulok.
1569: Ayutthaya falls again to Bayinnaung.
1584: Raja Hijau of Patani acknowledges Siamese authority.
May 1584: Naresuan proclaims Ayutthaya's independence and the Northern Cities return.
1591: Siam invades Cambodia.
1593: Naresuan takes the Tenasserim coast.
1594: the Mon provinces become Siamese.
3 January 1594: Naresuan storms Longvek.
1594: Cambodia passes under Ayutthaya's suzerainty.
January 1595: Naresuan marches on Pegu with 120,000 men.
1600: Lan Na comes into Siam's orbit.
May 1600: Naresuan gives up the campaign.
1613: Burma takes Tavoy ('1613 Burma takes Tavoy').
1618: the treaty gives Lan Na to Burma.
1618: the Mon provinces are back under Burma by the Cliopatria shape of 1619 (222 cells).
1618: Cambodia stops paying tribute.
1633: Ayutthaya attacks Patani and fails.
1634: the attack on Patani ends without gain ('Siam failed to take Patani').
February 1663: Narai takes Chiang Mai.
1663: the Siamese leave Lan Na 'later that year' because of a rebellious populace (no month on the page).
November 1663: Narai invades Burma in three columns.
1664: the Siamese retreat.

c. 1680: the court moves to Lopburi. The infobox: Lopburi 'early 1680s-1688'; the year is a placeholder for 'early 1680s'. Narai page (read 2026-10-19): no year for the move ('arguably prompted by the Dutch naval blockade of Ayutthaya in 1664'); Narai is at his Lopburi palaces in 1685 and in March 1688.
1688: Patani refuses Phetracha.
1688: the capital returns to Ayutthaya (infobox: Ayutthaya 1688-1767); Phetracha took the throne and was crowned on 1 August 1688.
1715: Ayutthaya invades Cambodia against Vietnamese backing.
1717 (end not dated by any page): the second Siamese invasion of 1717 ends and the Siamese withdraw.
December 1759: Alaungpaya invades.
1760: Burma keeps Dawei and upper Tenasserim.
May 1760: the war ends with Alaungpaya's death near Martaban; Ayutthaya 'was thus saved from Burmese conquest' for seven years.
1765: the rest of Tenasserim goes to Burma.
23 August 1765: the last Burmese invasion begins.
7 April 1767: the war ends with the fall of Ayutthaya (the war page runs 23 August 1765 - 7 April 1767).
7 April 1767: Ayutthaya falls.

wars.name: Ayutthaya-Angkor war (1352-1357)
wars.outcome: Angkor was besieged in 1352 and captured the next year; Siamese princes were set on the Khmer throne until Suryavamsa Rajadhiraja retook it in 1357.

wars.name: Siamese capture of Angkor (1393-1394)
wars.outcome: Ramesuan besieged Angkor in 1393 and captured it in 1394; the page does not say how long it was held.

wars.name: Siamese attacks on Angkor (1431-1433)
wars.outcome: Ayutthaya attacked Angkor, did not sack it on the Ayutthaya page and installed a short-lived puppet ruler; the Khmer court left Angkor for Phnom Penh.

wars.name: Ayutthaya-Lan Na War
wars.outcome: Stalemate; Lan Na 'achieved limited territorial gains' and ended the war by retaking Chienjuen in 1474.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1547-1549)
wars.outcome: The Burmese siege of Ayutthaya failed.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1563-1564)
wars.outcome: Bayinnaung took the Northern Cities (Kamphaeng Phet on 4 December 1563), captured the Portuguese ships and batteries on 7 February 1564 and received the Siamese king's surrender on 18 February 1564; Ayutthaya became his vassal.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1568-1569)
wars.outcome: Burmese victory: the city fell on 2 August 1569 and Mahathammarachathirat was made vassal king.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1584-1593)
wars.outcome: Naresuan proclaimed independence in May 1584 and in 1593 killed Mingyi Swa in the elephant duel; Siam invaded Burma.

wars.name: Siamese-Cambodian War (1591-1594)
wars.outcome: Siamese victory: Pursat and Battambang fell in 1591, Longvek was stormed on 3 January 1594 and Cambodian royals were taken to Ayutthaya.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1593-1600)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: Siam took the Tenasserim coast (1593) and the Mon provinces (1594), besieged Pegu in 1595 and gave up at Toungoo in May 1600.

wars.name: Siamese expedition to Cambodia (1621-1622)
wars.outcome: 'A Siamese expedition in 1621-22 to reconquer Cambodia failed in dramatic fashion'; no border moved.

wars.name: Siamese attack on Patani (1633-1634)
wars.outcome: The Siamese failed to take Patani.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1662-1664)
wars.outcome: Burmese defensive victory: Narai held Chiang Mai from February 1663 to later that year and withdrew from Burma by May 1664; the Tenasserim cities fell back under Burmese rule almost at once.

wars.name: Siamese-Nguyen struggle for Cambodia (1715-1717)
wars.outcome: Disputed: the Ang Em page has the Siamese invasions of 1715 and 1717 fail and withdraw; the Siamese-Vietnamese wars table calls 1717 a Siamese victory.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1759-1760)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: Burma gained Dawei and upper Tenasserim but failed to take Ayutthaya; Alaungpaya died in May 1760.

wars.name: Burmese-Siamese War (1765-1767)
wars.outcome: Burmese victory: Ayutthaya fell on 7 April 1767 after a fourteen-month siege; Siam lost Tenasserim; Taksin reconquered the Ayutthaya-Thonburi area in November 1767.

certainty.note: A mandala of tributary cities with no treaty lines: the page's frontiers are cities and expeditions.
